transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (NovaAnalytics - Head of Search), Tom Baker (CTO), Priya Nair (ML Engineer)

Summary (auto): Initial discovery to understand NovaAnalytics' current embedding + reranking stack, requirements for throughput and latency, evaluation of Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for both experimentation and production, and plan to run benchmarks and security review.

Transcript:
00:00 Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to go through our current setup for semantic search and see how Redwood might fit, especially around reranking and embeddings throughput.
00:22 Maya: Awesome, thanks Lena. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood; Ethan's our solutions engineer. Could you give us a quick picture of current infra?
00:34 Lena: Sure, so we run a hybrid stack. We produce embeddings with an internal model — currently 1536 dims from an open model, store vectors in Pinecone for production, and use Elastic for lexical fallback. We do an initial ANN search then a rerank using a cross-encoder for top 50 candidates.
00:52 Tom: Also want to flag that compliance is important for us — SOC 2 in progress, and we'll need SAML SSO and VPC options for any private deployment.
01:08 Ethan: Totally. Two quick clarifying Qs: what's your current QPS for search queries and what latency SLO are you targeting for production rerank?
01:20 Priya: Avg QPS around 40 steady, spikes to ~150 during reports. For rerank we aim for p95 under 300ms end-to-end, ideally ~200ms for user-facing search.
01:34 Maya: Great, that helps. At a high level Redwood can support three approaches: Hosted (fast to onboard), Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable throughput and isolation), or Private (VPC/air-gapped). For embeddings/rerank we also have integrated features like streaming, prefix caching, and model variants optimized for throughput vs quality.
01:52 Lena: When you say integrated, do you mean Redwood can replace both Pinecone and the cross-encoder stage? Or just provide embeddings and model hosting?
02:06 Ethan: Good question — Redwood can provide embeddings and model inference for reranking. For vector DB, we integrate with existing vendors via our ingestion connectors and also support direct storage and ANN indexes on Dedicated. Many teams keep Pinecone or Milvus and use Redwood for the model scoring/rerank step. We also support hybrid search patterns: ANN candidate generation + lexical re-rank or per-token rerank on the runtime.
02:32 Tom: Curious about dimensionality. We're on 1536 dims now — any guidance on reducing dims or quantization? Tradeoffs?
02:44 Ethan: Yes — higher dims tend to give better semantic signal but increase storage and ANN index cost. We often see 768–1536 as sweet spot. For production you can quantize embeddings (8-bit/IVF+PQ) to reduce storage; Redwood's recommendations depend on recall targets. For rerank, the cross-encoder step benefits from higher-quality embeddings for candidates, but the heavy lifting is done by the reranker model which we can run in a faster quantized mode on Dedicated GPUs.
03:12 Priya: For hybrid search we currently do HNSW with Pinecone. Would integrating Redwood rerank add much latency? We're worried about p95 spikes.
03:26 Ethan: It depends on deployment. Hosted is multi-tenant so latency is great for prototyping but offers less predictability under bursty spikes. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity — predictable p95s and can be tuned with batching and KV cache. Private gives you full control, VPC peering, and on-prem if you need it. For your p95 target (~200–300ms), Dedicated or Private is likely the fit for production rerank at your QPS profile.
03:52 Lena: And what about throughput? If we need to rerank top 50 for 150 QPS spikes that's 7.5k evals/s — is that realistic?
04:04 Ethan: Reranking cost depends on the model size and whether you do full cross-encoder or a lighter scorer. For full cross-encoder at that scale you'd need batching across GPUs; Redwood Dedicated supports continuous batching and kernel optimizations. We typically recommend a smaller cross-encoder or two-stage scoring: cheap bi-encoder re-score then cross-encoder for final N. With batching and optimized kernels we can hit thousands of evaluations per second on a multi-GPU pool. We'll propose exact sizing after we see sample queries and the model choice.
04:36 Tom: I also want to understand persistence and vector DB choices. If we keep Pinecone, how tightly does Redwood integrate? Is it simply pull vectors and call rerank?
04:48 Ethan: Integrations are straightforward — Redwood can call your vector DB to get candidate IDs and scores, fetch the payload or text from your DB via batch API, then run rerank. Alternatively, we can host embeddings and the ANN indexes on Dedicated which often reduces overall latency since the rerank model and ANN index can be co-located. We support S3 backfills, streaming ingestion, and connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, FAISS-based stores, and we have a generic vector API.
05:20 Priya: Any gotchas with index types — we use HNSW but see recall drop with quantized vectors.
05:30 Ethan: HNSW is great; quantization (PQ/OPQ) can hurt recall depending on vector distribution. Another pattern: keep high-quality vectors for rerank candidates (store full-precision in an archival store) and use quantized indexes for fast candidate gen. We'll include recommended index configs in the follow-up.
05:52 Lena: Security — you mentioned audit logs and KMS? We need full encryption at rest and customer-managed keys ideally.
06:04 Maya: Yep — Private and Dedicated support KMS/HSM integrations. Hosted offers encryption at rest and in transit; for CMKs we do Dedicated/Private. Audit logs, RBAC, SSO/SAML, and fine-grained ACLs are available for enterprise customers. We'll attach SOC 2 and ISO docs.
06:22 Tom: Good, that's helpful. On pricing — what's the hosted cost vs dedicated? Also does Redwood charge per-token for rerank?
06:34 Maya: Pricing depends on model usage and deployment: Hosted is usage-based (per inference / per-token or per-eval depending on model). Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) plus usage for extra. For rerank it's often billed per-eval or per-second of GPU if on Dedicated; we'll send a detailed breakdown comparing typical costs for a top-50 rerank at your QPS.
06:58 Priya: For prototype we'd like Hosted to iterate quickly then move to Dedicated. Any friction migrating models or config?
07:10 Ethan: Migration is smooth — same API and rollout abstractions across modes. You can pin model versions, run canary rollouts, and route by policy (latency/cost). We provide SDKs and infra templates to replicate the Dedicated setup.
07:26 Lena: About experiments — we'll probably run an A/B between current Pinecone+cross-encoder and Redwood rerank. Do you support evaluation harnesses / regressions?
07:38 Maya: Yes we have Redwood Optimize which gives quality monitoring, evals on prompt sets, and regression alerts. We can hook your test queries and track MRR/recall changes over time.
07:52 Tom: Network architecture for Private — we need VPC peering and strict egress rules. How do you handle that?
08:02 Ethan: For Private we can deploy a control plane that talks only over peered VPCs or a customer-managed control plane. We support private link/VPC peering, and for on-prem we have an air-gapped package. We'll share network diagrams in the next email.
08:20 Priya: Any live customer examples of similar scale?
08:26 Maya: Yes, a fintech customer with ~100 QPS peak uses Dedicated with HNSW candidate gen + two-stage rerank. We can anonymize and share their benchmark results and sizing.
08:40 Lena: On embedding dimensionality again — if we switch to 768 dims we drop storage but maybe hit recall. Do you run automatic recommendations per workload?
08:52 Ethan: Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and model variants based on your recall targets and latency curve. We'll run a pilot and generate per-workload recommendations.
09:06 Tom: Let's talk telemetry — what does Redwood expose? We need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency.
09:16 Maya: Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost/latency breakdowns, traces, and error analysis. For Dedicated we can also stream logs to your SIEM and set retention windows.
09:34 Priya: For benchmarks — what's the typical format you need? QPS profile, sample queries, expected ground-truth?
09:44 Ethan: Exactly — sample dataset (10-50k vectors), ground-truth relevancy for a subset (for MRR/Recall), QPS profile (steady + burst), and typical query lengths. We'll use that to size Dedicated nodes and simulate p95s.
10:00 Lena: Okay, that sounds good. Any immediate red flags on our side? We're concerned about cost and migration time.
10:12 Maya: Migration risk is manageable; start with Hosted for experimenting with the reranker and then lift-and-shift to Dedicated once you have steady QPS. Cost-wise, reranking top 50 is expensive if you run heavyweight cross-encoders; we'll suggest hybrid scoring and smaller full-encoder passes.
10:32 Tom: Does Redwood provide model hosting for customer models or only Redwood-verified models? For privacy we'd prefer hosting our own rerank models.
10:42 Ethan: We support customer-managed models on Dedicated and Private, plus bring-your-own-model flows. Hosted can host customer models under private tenancy depending on contract. We'll note the options in the follow-up.
11:00 Priya: A few quick technical Qs — do you support streaming rerank (token-level) or only batch candidate scoring?
11:10 Ethan: We support streaming outputs and function/tool calling; for rerank it's typically batch scoring of candidates. Token-level streaming is more for generation tasks, not for cross-encoder rerankers.
11:26 Lena: Any limits on model size for Dedicated? Like can we run a 7B cross-encoder quantized?
11:36 Ethan: Yes, Dedicated supports large models and quantized formats. We usually recommend 7B for middle-ground; 70B is possible but costs jump. We'll advise on performance/cost tradeoffs in the sizing document.
11:56 Tom: Let's plan tangible next steps — we'll send sample dataset and set up a benchmark week. Also need SSO/security paperwork.
12:08 Maya: Perfect. To recap: Redwood will send pricing and sizing, SE will set benchmark plan and request sample data, NovaAnalytics will share dataset and SSO/security contacts. We'll also schedule a follow-up technical deep dive for Private networking.
12:26 Lena: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
12:30 Meeting end.
